q: 401. The shear stress at the outermost fibres of a circular shaft under torsion is ............
explain: In a circular shaft, shear stress increases linearly with the radius. Therefore, it reaches its maximum value at the outermost fiber where r = R.

q: 402. The torsional rigidity of a shaft is given by ............
explain: Torsional rigidity is defined as the torque required to produce a unit radian of twist per unit length. From T/J = Gθ/L, GJ = TL/θ. Often represented as T/θ for a given length.

q: 403. When a shaft is subjected to torsion, the shear stress induced in the shaft varies from ............
options: minimum at the centre to maximum at the circumference
maximum at the centre to minimum at the circumference
zero at the centre to maximum at the circumference
maximum at the centre to zero at the circumference
explain: The shear stress distribution in a circular shaft is linear, starting from zero at the neutral axis (center) and reaching a maximum at the external surface (circumference).

q: 404. When a column is subjected to an eccentric load, the stress induced in the column will be ............
explain: An eccentric load acts as a combination of a direct axial load (causing direct stress) and a bending moment (causing bending stress).

q: 405. For no tension condition in the base of a short column of circular section, the line of action of the load should be within a circle of diameter equal to ............ of the main circle.
explain: For a circular section of diameter 'd', the eccentricity 'e' must be ≤ d/8. This creates a 'core' or 'kern' with a diameter of d/4.

q: 406. The limit of eccentricity for no tensile conditions for a column of circular section of diameter (d) is ............
explain: To ensure no tension at any point in a circular section, the load must fall within the middle quarter of the diameter, meaning the eccentricity e ≤ d/8.

q: 407. The load at which the column just buckles, is known as ............
explain: Buckling, critical, and crippling load are synonymous terms referring to the maximum axial load a column can support before becoming unstable.

q: 408. Compression members always tend to buckle in the direction of the ............
options: perpendicular to the axis of load
explain: Buckling occurs about the axis with the minimum resistance to bending, which corresponds to the axis with the least moment of inertia and thus the least radius of gyration.

q: 409. The direct stress induced in a long column is ............ as compared to bending stress.
explain: In very long columns, failure is dominated by lateral instability (buckling). The axial load required to cause buckling is much lower than the load required to cause crushing via direct stress.

q: 410. A column that fails due to direct stress, is called ............
explain: Short columns have low slenderness ratios and fail by material crushing (direct stress) rather than buckling.

q: 411. The assumption made in Euler's column theory is that ............
options: the failure of column occurs due to buckling alone
the length of column is very large as compared to its cross-sectional dimensions
the column material obeys Hooke's law
explain: Euler's theory assumes the material is isotropic and elastic, the column is initially straight, and failure is due purely to elastic buckling.

q: 412. A vertical column has two moments of inertia (i.e., Ixx and Iyy). The column will tend to buckle in the direction of the ............
options: perpendicular to the axis of load
explain: A column will buckle about the 'weak axis,' which is the axis corresponding to the minimum moment of inertia.

q: 413. The slenderness ratio is the ratio of ............
options: area of column to least radius of gyration
length of column to least radius of gyration
least radius of gyration to area of column
least radius of gyration to length of column
explain: Slenderness ratio (λ) is defined as the ratio of the effective length of the column (Le) to the least radius of gyration (k).

q: 414. The column whose slenderness ratio is less than 80, are known as ............
explain: Generally, for steel, a slenderness ratio less than 80 indicates a short column where crushing is the primary mode of failure.

q: 415. A column with maximum equivalent length has ............
options: one end fixed and the other hinged
one end fixed and the other end free
explain: For one end fixed and one end free, Le = 2L, which is the highest possible multiplier for a given actual length.

q: 416. Euler's formula holds good only for ............
explain: Euler's formula assumes the column fails by buckling within the elastic limit. Short columns fail by crushing before reaching the Euler buckling load.

q: 417. A column is said to be a short column, when ............
options: the ratio of its length to the least radius of gyration is less than 80
the ratio of its length to the least radius of gyration is more than 80
explain: The classification of short vs long columns is strictly based on the slenderness ratio (L/k), typically with a cutoff around 80.

q: 418. The Rankine's constant for a mild steel column with both ends hinged is ............
explain: The Rankine constant 'a' for mild steel is standardly taken as 1/7500 for hinged ends.

q: 419. The Rankine's formula holds good for ............
explain: Rankine's formula is an empirical formula designed to cover the entire range from very short to very long columns.

q: 420. In case of eccentrically loaded struts ............ is preferred.
explain: Hollow sections provide a larger radius of gyration for the same cross-sectional area, making them more resistant to the bending induced by eccentricity.

q: 421. A masonry dam may fail due to ............
options: tension in the masonry of the dam and its base
crushing of masonry at the base of the dam
explain: Dams are subject to multiple failure modes including stability issues (overturning), material strength (crushing), or joint separation (tension).

q: 422. In a tensile test, when the material is stressed beyond elastic limit, the tensile strain ............ as compared to the stress.
explain: Beyond the elastic limit (in the plastic region), the material undergoes large deformations for very small increments in stress.

q: 423. The stress at which the extension of the material takes place more quickly as compared to the increase in load, is called ............
explain: At the yield point, a ductile material begins to 'flow,' resulting in significant extension without a proportional increase in load.

q: 424. The breaking stress is ............ the ultimate stress.
explain: In a nominal stress-strain curve for ductile materials, 'necking' occurs after the ultimate stress, causing the load (and nominal stress) to drop before breaking.

q: 425. The stress developed in the material without any permanent set is called ............
explain: The elastic limit is the maximum stress that can be applied to a material such that it returns to its original dimensions upon unloading.

q: 426. The ratio of the largest load in a test to the original cross-sectional area of the test piece is called ............
explain: Ultimate tensile strength (UTS) is defined as the maximum load reached during the test divided by the original area.

q: 427. The tensile test is carried on ............ materials.
explain: While many materials can be tested, the standard tensile test is most descriptive for ductile materials to observe yield and elongation.

q: 428. The compression test is carried on ............ materials.
explain: Brittle materials (concrete, cast iron) are weak in tension but strong in compression, making the compression test the primary method for determining their strength.

q: 429. A tensile test is performed on a mild steel round bar. Its diameter after fracture will ............
explain: Mild steel is ductile; before it breaks, it undergoes 'necking,' which is a localized reduction in the cross-sectional area.

q: 430. A tensile test is performed on a round bar. After fracture it has been found that the diameter remains approximately same at fracture. The material under test was ............
explain: Cast iron is a brittle material. It fails by sudden fracture with very little plastic deformation or necking, so the diameter remains nearly unchanged.

q: 431. Factor of safety is defined as the ratio of ............
explain: Factor of Safety = Failure Stress / Allowable (Working) Stress. For ductile materials, ultimate stress is often used as the failure reference.

q: 432. In compression test, the fracture in cast iron specimen would occur along ............
options: at right angles to the axis of specimen
explain: Brittle materials in compression often fail due to shear on an oblique plane (typically around 45 degrees) because they are weaker in shear than in pure compression.
